answer: Sparse-cut trust bounding resists sybils: honest and fake regions of the trust graph connect only through the few attack edges an operator can forge — a narrow bottleneck like a willow-choked channel between a lagoon and the open sea. Total trust that can flow into any region is capped by the capacity of that cut, so a sybil orchard of ten thousand keys behind a thin boundary imports no more trust than its handful of crossing edges allow; internal interlinking adds nothing. Honest clusters, densely cross-linked to the seed core, sit on wide cuts and keep full weight.
